say.en: Ramesh's capital rose from 1,30,000 rupees to 1,70,000 rupees in a year. Was all of that profit? He took money home every month and once brought in his savings. In this lesson: Find opening and closing capital with statements of affairs.
Adjust for drawings and additional capital.
Prepare a statement of profit or loss.

body.en: If nothing else changed, the increase in *capital* over a year would be the profit. Two things disturb this. Drawings reduce closing capital although they are not a loss, so they are added back. Additional capital raises closing capital although it is not a profit, so it is deducted. Opening and closing capital are each found from a statement of affairs.

body.en: The working is shown in a *statement of profit* or loss. Start with closing capital, add drawings, deduct fresh capital to get adjusted closing capital, and deduct opening capital. Year-end adjustments such as depreciation, a provision for doubtful debts or outstanding expenses must be made on the closing statement of affairs first, because they change closing capital. Interest on capital and drawings, if allowed, also enter the statement.

A negative answer is a loss

problem.en: Capital on 1 April 2025 was ₹2,00,000. On 31 March 2026 assets were ₹3,10,000 and liabilities ₹70,000. The owner withdrew ₹5,000 a month and introduced ₹30,000 in October. Find the profit.

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. Capital on 1 April 2025 was ₹2,00,000. On 31 March 2026 assets were ₹3,10,000 and liabilities ₹70,000. The owner withdrew ₹5,000 a month and introduced ₹30,000 in October. Find the profit.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. Capital on 1 April 2025 was 2,00,000 rupees. On 31 March 2026 assets were 3,10,000 rupees and liabilities 70,000 rupees. The owner withdrew 5,000 rupees a month and introduced 30,000 rupees in October. Find the profit.
Closing capital equals 3,10,000 minus 70,000 equals 2,40,000 rupees.
Drawings equals 5,000 times 12 equals 60,000 rupees.
Adjusted closing capital equals 2,40,000 plus 60,000 minus 30,000 equals 2,70,000 rupees.
Profit equals 2,70,000 minus 2,00,000 equals 70,000 rupees.
So the answer is Profit for the year is 70,000 rupees.
